title: You Can't Live on Fun
about: A reflection on my final year as an Assistant Director and the difficult realization that loving the work wasn't enough to make the hours financially sustainable.
description: After taking a year away, I returned to State Arts-In in 2023 and stepped back into the Assistant Director role alongside Lauren and Jenna. I still loved the work, the people, and the strange rhythm of days that began around six in the morning and often continued long after the paid hours ended. Eventually, though, I had to acknowledge the practical reality behind something I genuinely enjoyed. Minimum wage for only part of an extremely long day could not support a future, no matter how meaningful the experience was. This song became the closing reflection on my years as an Assistant Director: leaving wasn't about losing love for SAI. It was about appreciating what those summers gave me while accepting that some things can be valuable without being sustainable.
lyrics: Verse 1
I had a year to walk away,
Then found my way right back again.
The office doors still felt the same,
Like I'd never really left back then.
Lauren, Jenna, side by side,
Another summer set to run.
The days were long, the work was real,
Another chapter had begun.
Pre-Chorus
The lights came on before the sun,
And somehow stayed till daylight's gone.
You don't count the hours there,
You just keep carrying on.
Chorus
You can't live on fun,
No matter how bright the memories become.
You can fill your heart with songs to sing,
Still have bills when the summer's done.
I'd do it all with all I had,
I'd smile through every early sun.
Some dreams pay you in moments...
You just can't live on fun.
Verse 2
Morning started around six o'clock,
Evening ended who knows when.
Every extra hour after that
Was simply given once again.
Nobody asked us why we stayed,
We never stopped to count the cost.
Because when you're building something special,
It's easy not to notice what's been lost.
Pre-Chorus
Every laugh made every hour
Feel lighter than it really was.
Sometimes love can hide the truth
Until reality shows up.
Chorus
You can't live on fun,
No matter how bright the memories become.
You can fill your heart with songs to sing,
Still have bills when the summer's done.
I'd do it all with all I had,
I'd smile through every early sun.
Some dreams pay you in moments...
You just can't live on fun.
Bridge
Leaving never meant I stopped believing.
It never meant the memories grew dim.
Sometimes growing up means thanking yesterday,
While knowing you can't keep living in it.
Final Chorus
You can't live on fun,
Though I wouldn't trade what we'd become.
Every sunrise, every late night,
Every challenge overcome.
My final year came quietly,
Without a grand goodbye or run.
I left with more than I arrived with...
Even if you can't live on fun.
Outro
Some places teach you who you are.
Some seasons eventually end.
I'll always be thankful for those summers...
And the people I called friends.
